analysis.title: GS Consumer | Morning Trading Update (US) 2 Oct 2026
key_insights: US equity futures are rallying (SPX +45bps, NDX +75bps, RTY +60bps) as Treasuries hold yesterday's gains: 2yr unchanged at 4.79%, 10yr -0.5bps at 5.235%, 30yr -0.5bps at 5.605%.
WTI crude is down 3.75% at $89.40 on reports European nations are weighing a release of diesel and crude stockpiles, with France reportedly suggesting 100mb.
Overnight inflation data was mixed: Eurozone headline CPI ran slightly hotter with core in line, and Tokyo CPI printed hot across the board.
Focus shifts to US September NFP and unemployment rate at 8:30am, plus Fed speakers Logan (voter, 10am) and Goolsbee (non-voter, 12pm). Pre-market earnings include CADE, EXAS, DAY and USDE.
NKE fell 8% (now down about 50% YTD) after another top-line miss and disappointing FY27 guidance. Weakness in Sportswear, Jordan and China outweighed continued strength in the performance business.

NKE FY27 EPS is guided to $1.15-$1.35 ex-items vs $1.68 consensus, with revenue down high-single digits vs consensus of down 2.3%. GS says FY27 is not far off what bears anticipated, and the open question is whether this is a trough the company can grow from, with no obvious evidence of that yet.

GS applies a 25x multiple to the $1.25 guidance midpoint to get a $31.25 NKE value, noting 25x is still full for a retail company with declining revenue, and that short positioning and recovery hope may keep the valuation elevated.
NKE introduced 'Pace', a new operating model targeting $2.5B in cumulative savings through FY31.

Tax-loss selling remains in focus. The GS basket tracking candidates (GSCBMF26) fell 9% in September, its second worst month of the year. October has a larger share of mutual fund year-ends than September, and many consumer stocks are down on the year.
GS Prime September update: the global book was modestly net sold, with short sales modestly outpacing long buys. Gross trading activity rose at the fastest pace since May.

Prime: single stocks were net sold (short sales outpaced long buys 1.2 to 1). Communication Services, Info Tech and Financials were the most net bought sectors. Industrials, Health Care and Staples were the most net sold.

Prime: Macro Products (index and ETF combined) were net bought, led by short covers. US-listed ETF shorts rose 4% in September, led by Credit and Small-Cap ETFs, and are 10.1% of the US equity short book ex-index products, in the 2nd percentile vs the past year and five years.

Prime, consumer: Discretionary was net sold with short sales outpacing long buys 1.5 to 1. Automobiles, Textiles/Apparel/Luxury and Household Durables were the most net sold subsectors. Specialty Retail and Hotels/Restaurants/Leisure were the most net bought.
US Consumer Discretionary long/short ratio is 2.06, a 1-year low and the 63rd percentile vs five years. Defensive sectors saw the largest % net selling in nearly a year.

September US auto SAAR was about 16.0mn per Motor Intelligence and Wards, slightly below the StreetAccount consensus of 16.1mn. Total sales rose about 4% y/y and fell 5% sequentially. Ford was up about 2% y/y and GM about flat.

September EV sales fell about 46% y/y (6% of volumes) and hybrids rose about 35% y/y. Incentive spending per vehicle fell about 8% y/y and inventory rose to about 2.71mn units. In 3Q26 total units fell 1% y/y and 4% q/q, with GM down 6% y/y and Ford down 7%.

GIR finds 3Q-to-date promotions in specialty hardlines mixed y/y: higher in store at Dick's and Academy (partly on later back-to-school timing) but lower online. Foot Locker promotional breadth rose and depth fell sequentially.
GIR reiterates Buy on DKS (health and wellness trends, share gains, higher structural margins, Foot Locker acquisition) and on ASO (expanded offerings, emerging unit growth, 7.0x NTM P/E).

Macau September GGR fell 1% y/y to MOP18.1bn, broadly in line with lowered expectations and at 82% of FY19 levels (vs 83% in July and 90% in August). 3Q26 GGR was MOP60.2bn (-1% q/q, -4% y/y), and YTD GGR is +3% y/y, in line with GIR's full-year forecast.
Next week's earnings include LW, STZ, LEVI, PEP and DAL, plus another consumer conference.

market_movers.rationale: Stock fell 8% after a top-line miss and FY27 EPS guide of $1.15-$1.35 vs $1.68 consensus. GS frames a $31.25 value at 25x the guidance midpoint.
GIR cites health and wellness trends, brand heat, share gains and structurally higher margins. A more promotional industry does not change its competitive position.
GIR cites expanded offerings, an emerging unit growth story and a 7.0x NTM P/E. The lifestyle footwear slowdown mostly affects mall-based chains.

Net sold in September as defensive sectors saw their largest % net selling in nearly a year.

earnings_insights: NKE reported FQ1 EPS $0.48 vs $0.44 consensus on revenue of $11.21B vs $11.32B consensus. Gross margin was 42.8% vs 42.4% consensus, helped by lower logistics costs.
NKE Greater China fell 26% ex-FX and North America grew 2%.
NKE FY27 guidance: EPS $1.15-$1.35 ex-items (consensus $1.68), revenue down high-single digits (consensus down 2.3%), reflecting margin pressure from deleverage.
Pre-market earnings on 10/2 include CADE, EXAS, DAY and USDE. Upcoming next week: LW, STZ, LEVI, PEP, DAL.
